title: Security posture discovery with Orion Ventures
summary: Introductory security posture discovery focused on hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment. Customer very focused on SOC 2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logging, KMS integration, and data residency/retention. Agreed next steps: share SOC 2/ISO docs, network diagram for Private, and schedule a Dedicated performance/FIPS crypto follow-up with SE.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
action_items: Jordan Hayes: Send SOC2 and ISO27001 attestation + security overview deck (due: 2026-07-02)
Priya Nair: Share technical docs on SSO/SAML setup and RBAC examples + Okta playbook (due: 2026-07-06)
Marcus Lee: Provide Dedicated capacity pricing and pilot agreement template (due: 2026-07-03)
Evan Park / Liam O'Connor: Share internal network diagram and list of required IP allowlists for Private deployment (due: 2026-07-09)
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2/ISO artifacts and security whitepaper
Customer to review hosted vs dedicated options internally and confirm preferred deployment for pilot
Schedule follow-up deep dive on KMS/HSM and FIPS requirements (SE-led) week of 2026-07-06
transcript:
00:00 Jordan Hayes: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, with Priya and Marcus. How's everyone doing?
00:07 Samantha Ruiz: Good morning, hi, thanks. We appreciate you making time.
00:11 Jordan Hayes: Yeah, great. Quick agenda - we want to understand your security and compliance requirements, current stack, who needs access, and constraints for hosted vs dedicated vs private. We'll also cover SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and encryption. Does that sound right?
00:24 Liam O'Connor: Yep, that's exactly it. We're evaluating Redwood for a pilot and security is our gating factor.
00:29 Priyanka Mehta: I have a short list: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, SSO integration with Okta, audit logs forward to our SIEM, and KMS integration - we may need an HSM or at least customer-managed keys.
00:41 Priya Nair: Thanks Priyanka. Quick clarifier on our side: Redwood offers Hosted (our cloud API), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools for a customer), and Private (VPC or on-prem). Hosted is fastest but we understand customers sometimes require dedicated or private for data residency or KMS requirements.
00:57 Samantha Ruiz: Right, our legal and GRC folks will push hard for a private deployment if they can't get customer-managed keys in hosted. Can you walk through where keys are stored in hosted?
01:06 Priya Nair: Sure. For hosted we encrypt at rest using provider-managed KMS by default; we have support for bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via customer-managed KMS for certain enterprise plans - the Dedicated tier and Private deployments have more options for full customer key control. Note - some auto-transcription of product names, apologies, sometimes it comes out as Redwood Devoted in notes.
01:28 Samantha Ruiz: (laughs) That's fine. Can you confirm whether BYOK integrates with AWS KMS and whether HSM-backed keys are supported?
01:35 Priya Nair: Yes AWS KMS is supported; we also support Azure Key Vault for Private deployments. HSM-backed keys are supported via customer-managed KMS providers that expose HSM protection (YubiHSM, AWS CloudHSM). For FIPS or specialized crypto, we usually recommend Private or Dedicated with specific compliance add-on - we can put Priya on a technical session about FIPS-level requirements.
01:52 Liam O'Connor: Good. Another requirement - we need audit logs for all API calls, admin actions, model version rollouts, and RBAC changes, forwarded in near-real-time to our SIEM with retention of 7 years for certain logs. How granular are your logs?
02:09 Marcus Lee: We capture token-level billing and latency traces internally, and admin/audit events for RBAC and role changes. We can stream logs to a customer-owned S3 or via syslog/HTTPS to Splunk/Datadog; retention policies can be configured on the destination. For Hosted, we can set up secure log forwarding; for Private you control retention entirely.
02:28 Priyanka Mehta: So for hosted, logs leave your environment to our SIEM - is there an encryption in transit guarantee?
02:33 Priya Nair: Yes TLS 1.2+ for log shipping; we also support mTLS where needed.
02:39 Samantha Ruiz: Ok. On RBAC: we need fine-grained roles, least privilege, and integration with our SSO groups. How does Redwood handle RBAC primitives?
02:48 Priya Nair: We support SSO via SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is role-based with built-in roles like Admin, Developer, Billing, and you can create custom roles with granular permissions (model deploy, read logs, run evals). SCIM lets you sync groups from Okta so access is managed from your identity provider.
03:05 Evan Park: Are attribute-based access controls supported? e.g., allow certain users only to call hosted API with rate limits?
03:12 Priya Nair: We have policy controls and per-api keys with scopes - you can set per-key quotas and tie them to roles. ABAC is on our roadmap - right now most customers use RBAC + per-route API keys and network controls.
03:27 Samantha Ruiz: Data residency - some of our workloads must store data in EU only. Can Redwood guarantee region isolation on Hosted?
03:35 Jordan Hayes: For Hosted we have region options and can pin data to certain regions for enterprise customers; Dedicated and Private provide stronger isolation guarantees - with Private you can keep everything in your VPC in the EU. We'll include our data residency guide in the follow-up.
03:48 Liam O'Connor: What's your retention default for logs and model inputs? We can't have training data retained indefinitely for privacy reasons.
03:57 Marcus Lee: By default we retain logs for 90 days for hosted telemetry; customer data retention and deletion policies can be defined in the contract. For Dedicated, we can adjust retention and for Private you manage it. We do not use customer prompts to train our models in hosted unless a customer opts in for analytics; by default hosted does not persist inputs for model retraining - but we'll send the exact language from the privacy policy.
04:19 Samantha Ruiz: Great, can you explain how audit trails show content? We need redaction or hashing for PII fields in logs.
04:27 Priya Nair: Audit logs include metadata (request id, timestamp, user, model, route) and can include request/response bodies if enabled. We offer a redaction pipeline and can hash or tokenise PII before shipping. This is commonly done via our prefix filtering and webhook pipeline. We'll document the options.
04:44 Liam O'Connor: Network-level controls: do you offer IP allowlists for API calls, private links, or VPC peering?
04:51 Marcus Lee: Yes - Hosted supports IP allowlists on customer keys, and we offer PrivateLink-like connectivity for Dedicated and Private deployments; Private includes VPC peering and full customer-managed networking. We'll need your egress/ingress IP ranges for allowlist setup.
05:05 Priyanka Mehta: On compliance certifications - can you provide SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate? Also SAR issues - do you have pen test evidence?
05:15 Jordan Hayes: We can share SOC 2 Type II attestation and ISO 27001 certificate under an NDA; we also have a quarterly penetration testing cadence and can provide summary findings. I'll attach the artifacts.
05:27 Samantha Ruiz: Do you encrypt model weights at rest and provide key rotation?
05:32 Priya Nair: Model weights are encrypted at rest; key rotation is supported via your KMS for BYOK and automatic rotation for Redwood-managed keys. For Dedicated and Private you can define rotation policies in your KMS.
05:44 Liam O'Connor: In terms of separation of duties, who has access to customer data in your ops team?
05:49 Marcus Lee: Access is strictly role-based; production SREs have limited tooling and require ticket-based approvals for sensitive actions. We also have audit logging on operator actions. We'll include our access control and SOD doc.
06:02 Samantha Ruiz: Any limitations around GDPR data subject requests or data deletion timelines?
06:08 Jordan Hayes: We support DSAR workflows; for hosted we can remove data per contract and provide attestations. Private deployments let you fully control deletion. We'll share the legal playbook.
06:19 Evan Park: About model rollouts: we need a safe rollback mechanism and traces for which model version served which request for compliance auditing.
06:26 Priya Nair: Our rollout system tracks model versions and can tag rollouts with metadata; audit logs include model_version for each request. Canary rollouts, A/B and automatic fallback are supported; we'll show the tracing view in the Console demo.
06:40 Samantha Ruiz: One more - forensic readiness. If we detect an incident, how quickly can we get logs and are they tamper-evident?
06:48 Marcus Lee: We sign logs and support write-once storage options for critical logs. For incident response we have an SLA for log access in enterprise packages. We'll include our IR playbook and RTO/RPO for logs.
07:03 Liam O'Connor: Are there any open limitations with multi-tenancy in Hosted we should worry about?
07:09 Priya Nair: Hosted is multi-tenant but isolated at the request and data plane level - logical isolation, strict RBAC, per-tenant encryption keys for BYOK where applicable. For the strictest isolation we recommend Dedicated (single-tenant pools) or Private. We'll map this in the follow-up doc.
07:24 Samantha Ruiz: Pricing question: is Dedicated required for BYOK or can hosted with enterprise add-on do BYOK?
07:31 Jordan Hayes: BYOK is part of our enterprise-hosted offering for some customers; however Dedicated or Private give the clearest isolation guarantees and easier compliance sign-off - we'll provide a decision matrix showing tradeoffs.
07:43 Priyanka Mehta: We also need to know SLAs for uptime, request latency SLOs, and support escalation.
07:50 Marcus Lee: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; Hosted has best-effort SLAs with premium support add-ons. We'll include the SLA table and escalation path.
07:59 Evan Park: Ok, for the pilot we expect to run a small workload in EU region with BYOK and log forwarding to our Splunk instance. Is that doable?
08:09 Priya Nair: Totally doable. Pilot approach: start with Hosted enterprise with BYOK and log forwarding, if GRC still needs more isolation we can move to Dedicated or Private.
08:19 Samantha Ruiz: Timing - we need to present to our CISO and procurement in two weeks. Any blockers?
08:25 Jordan Hayes: We'll get artifacts out in 48 hours (SOC 2, ISO, network diagram requirements). SE deep dive next week for KMS/FIPS as requested.
08:33 Priyanka Mehta: If you can include examples of the SCIM mapping and sample RBAC policies that would be very helpful.
08:40 Priya Nair: Yep we'll include a sample Okta SAML metadata, SCIM mapping doc, and sample JSON for custom roles.
08:48 Samantha Ruiz: Great. Anything else from your side?
08:51 Liam O'Connor: No. Just curious about backup encryption and cross-region replication - need to ensure backups stay in the EU.
08:58 Marcus Lee: Backups respect region controls for Dedicated/Private; for Hosted we can enable EU-only backup policies for enterprise customers. We'll document replication controls.
09:11 Jordan Hayes: All right, quick recap and actions: Jordan send SOC2/ISO and security deck; Priya send SSO/SCIM and RBAC examples; Marcus send pricing for Dedicated pilot; customer to share network diagram. Any final Qs?
09:26 Samantha Ruiz: No, thanks everyone. We'll review and reconvene after receiving docs.
09:31 Jordan Hayes: Thanks, we'll follow up.
09:33 [call ends]
